history.ask: Change in bowel habit or unintentional weight loss

options: Thalassemia / chronic anemia in the family
Numbness or tingling in the feet

history.ask: Episodes of jaundice or dark urine

options: Low mood with loss of interest and poor sleep

red_flags: Melena, hematemesis, or any overt bleeding
Dyspnea at rest, chest pain, or syncope with pallor — decompensating anemia
Pallor with fever, bruising, or petechiae — marrow failure until excluded
exam: Inspect conjunctivae and palmar creases for pallor
Examine nails and mouth: koilonychia, angular stomatitis, smooth red tongue
Search the skin for petechiae and bruising
Auscultate: resting tachycardia, apical flow murmur
Posterior-column screen: vibration sense at the ankles, Romberg, gait
Feel the thyroid and test ankle-reflex relaxation
Digital rectal examination when GI blood loss is suspected
Record weight and compare with previous visits

investigations.why: The branch point: microcytic (iron deficiency / thalassemia), macrocytic (B12 deficiency), or normocytic (chronic disease, CKD, hemolysis, marrow failure) — and confirms whether anemia exists at all
Target cells support thalassemia; spherocytes or fragments support hemolysis; hypersegmented neutrophils support B12 deficiency; blasts or pancytopenia flag marrow disease
Low ferritin rules iron deficiency in; normal or high ferritin in a microcytic patient pushes toward thalassemia trait or anemia of chronic disease

investigations.test: Reticulocyte count with indirect bilirubin & LDH
investigations.why: High reticulocytes with raised indirect bilirubin/LDH rule hemolysis (or active bleeding) in; low reticulocytes mean underproduction
Confirms thalassemia when microcytosis persists with normal ferritin — essential in Iraq's carrier-prevalent population and for family counseling
Raised creatinine rules anemia of chronic kidney disease in
Raised TSH rules hypothyroidism in as the cause of fatigue with or without mild anemia
Hookworm ova explain iron deficiency; positive occult blood points to a GI source — ulcer or tumor
Confirms deficiency when macrocytosis, glossitis, or posterior-column signs are present
Second-line — iron deficiency in a man or postmenopausal woman is a GI lesion until proven otherwise: rules ulcer and colorectal or gastric malignancy in or out

supports: Heavy periods, poor diet, or pica
Regular NSAID use or bleeding hemorrhoids
Family history of anemia or consanguinity
Numbness, unsteady gait in the dark, sore tongue
Impaired vibration sense with positive Romberg
Known chronic inflammation, TB, or chronic infection
Episodes of jaundice or dark urine

differentials.dx: Occult gastrointestinal blood loss (ulcer or malignancy)
supports: Black stool or positive DRE finding
Change in bowel habit or weight loss after age 50
Low mood, loss of interest, poor sleep
No pallor and a normal examination
